title: Like an Olive Tree in the House of God
superscription: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, "David has gone to the house of Ahimelech."

verses.text: Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The loving devotion of God endures all day long.
Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.
You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth. Selah
You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue.
Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying,
"Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction."
But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.
I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name— for it is good— in the presence of Your saints.

context.author: The title names David. In Book Two, Psalms 51-65 are all “of David,” and several titles tie them to events in his life.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: The title sets it after “Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.” David, fleeing Saul, had received bread and Goliath’s sword from Ahimelech the priest at Nob; Doeg, Saul’s chief herdsman, saw it, reported it, and at Saul’s order killed eighty-five priests and the people of Nob (1 Samuel 21:1-9; 22:9-19). “Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man?” (v.1). “Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor” (v.2). God will uproot him “from the land of the living” (v.5). The righteous will say, “Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth” (v.7). “But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever” (v.8).
context.custom: Olive trees live for centuries and stay green all year, a picture of lasting life (Jeremiah 11:16). Trees grew in the courts of some ancient temples. Informers who reported to kings were feared, and a single report could destroy a town.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 53 is a second version of Psalm 14: “The fool says in his heart, There is no God.”
context.timelineBible: Only Abiathar escaped the massacre at Nob, and David took responsibility: “I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house” (1 Samuel 22:22). James warns that the tongue “is a fire” (James 3:6). Paul pictures believers grafted into God’s olive tree (Romans 11:17).

translation.meaning: Olive tree, olive; a picture of fruitfulness and long life.

gospelParallels.note: The rich man who stored up treasure.

otBackground.note: Doeg reports to Saul and kills the priests of Nob.
A green olive tree, beautiful in fruit.
He who trusts in his riches will fall.

mapCoords.placeName: Nob, the city of priests (location uncertain)

overview.summary: Against Doeg, the boasting informer who caused the massacre at Nob, David declares that God will uproot the deceitful, while he flourishes like an olive tree in God’s house.
overview.settingLine: The massacre at the city of priests.
overview.placeName: Nob, the city of priests (location uncertain)

history.t: A town of priests near Jerusalem.

archaeology.t: Some olive trees in Israel are over a thousand years old.
Its site is uncertain; Isaiah 10:32 places it within sight of Jerusalem.

overview.discussion: Doeg “did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth” (v.7). What do I make my refuge?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-100 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
overview.genre: Judgment on a boaster, and trust
